# Review: 7.2 CIP Sequence

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | Whole section | Not testable. No requirement IDs and no test method. | Add FR-CIP-NNN IDs and a FAT method for each. |
| R-02 | Steps 1-4 | Numbers are in prose (5, 20, 15 min; 65 C). | Move to a setpoint list. Reference by name. |
| R-03 | Step 1, 3 | "Open the rinse tank valve" has no tag. "To drain" has no valve, pump, or end condition. | Use tags. Define the end condition with CT-501 and a timeout. |
| R-04 | Step 2 | "Heated to temperature" is undefined. No temperature instrument or setpoint is named. The timer start is unclear. | Heat to the caustic temperature setpoint. Start the timer only when TT-501 and FT-501 are both in range. |
| R-05 | Step 2, 4 | No concentration check, no chemical recovery or drain rule, and no phase separation between rinse and chemical. | Use CT-501 to check concentration and to control the rinse/chemical cut. |
| R-06 | Step 4 | Acid temperature (65 C) is stated as an outcome only. No heating or control is defined. | Use the acid temperature setpoint and the same timer-start rule as Step 2. |
| R-07 | Step 5 | "Run until clean" cannot be tested. | End on the CT-501 rinse-complete setpoint, held for a set time, with a timeout. |
| R-08 | Steps 1-5 | No timeout or failure response per step. | Use the step table with both columns. |
| R-09 | Return pump line | "Operator should check" is not a requirement. P-501 can overfill the return line if P-502 stops. | Define a P-502 fault response: stop P-501, go to Hold, alarm. Define the restart conditions. |
| R-10 | Last line | "Any circuit selected" has no permissives. The draft does not prove that S-1 or HTST-1 is out of production. It does not require mix-proof valve position feedback or limit the run to one circuit. This is a product-safety risk. | Add start permissives and a lock on circuit selection during a run. |
| R-11 | Missing | No ISA-106 states, transitions, hold, abort, or automation level. | Add the state table. |
| R-12 | Missing | No abnormal handling for bad PV (FT-501, CT-501, TT-501), comms loss, power loss and restart, or fail positions. | Add a section with these cases. |
| R-13 | Missing | No operator interface, alarm reference, interlock reference, or open items. | Add them. Reference the C&E chart and alarm database. Do not restate their logic. |
| R-14 | Missing | The draft does not say whether the mix-proof leak and product-separation functions are SIS. | Reference the SRS if they are SIS. If not, state this and have the C&E chart own them. |
| R-15 | Wording | Passive and vague phrases ("is heated", "should check"). | Use imperative, active STE sentences. |

## Corrected section

### 7.2 CIP Sequence

**7.2.1 Boundaries.** The CIP skid cleans one circuit at a time: raw milk silo S-1 or pasteurizer HTST-1. The operator selects the circuit on the HMI. Circuits are routed through mix-proof valves. Valve tags are in the instrument index.

**7.2.2 States and transitions (SBC)**

| State | Entry permissive | Allowed exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Idle | None | Checking | Operator | Manual |
| Checking | Circuit selected | Running, Idle | Auto | Automatic |
| Running | All start permissives true (FR-CIP-003) | Holding, Aborting, Complete | Auto | Automatic |
| Holding | Hold command or fault | Running, Aborting | Auto or operator | Operator-prompted |
| Aborting | Abort command or abort fault | Idle | Auto or operator | Automatic |
| Complete | Step 6 done | Idle | Auto | Automatic |

**7.2.3 Requirements**

| ID | Requirement | FAT test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-CIP-001 | Allow one circuit selection at a time. | Select both circuits. Verify the second is rejected. |
| FR-CIP-002 | Lock the circuit selection while the state is not Idle. | Change the selection during a run. Verify it is rejected. |
| FR-CIP-003 | Allow start only when all permissives in the C&E chart are true. These include the selected circuit being out of production and the mix-proof valves being in the CIP lineup. | Force each permissive false. Verify no start. |
| FR-CIP-004 | Start each timed step timer only when TT-501 and FT-501 are in the ranges in the setpoint list. | Hold TT-501 low. Verify the timer does not run. |
| FR-CIP-005 | Use CT-501 to decide the end of rinse steps and to check chemical strength. | Simulate CT-501 values. Verify each transition. |
| FR-CIP-006 | If P-502 stops, stop P-501, go to Holding, and raise the alarm in the alarm database. | Trip P-502 in each step. Verify the response. |
| FR-CIP-007 | Allow Holding to Running only after the operator acknowledges and the permissives are true. The step resumes from its start. | Clear the fault. Verify no auto-resume. |
| FR-CIP-008 | Go to Aborting on abort command or step timeout. Close the chemical supply, then stop P-501 and P-502. | Time out a step. Verify the abort. |

**7.2.4 Sequence (SqBC)**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Pre-rinse | Open the rinse tank outlet valve `<tag>`. Start P-502, then P-501. Route return to drain. | Pre-rinse time (SP-01) done, and CT-501 at or below SP-02 | SP-03 | Holding |
| 2 Caustic wash | Route supply from the caustic tank `<tag>`. Heat to SP-04. Circulate. | TT-501 at or above SP-05 and FT-501 at or above SP-06. Then the caustic time (SP-07) is done. | SP-08 | Holding. Abort if the timeout expires. |
| 3 Intermediate rinse | Route supply from the rinse tank. Route return to drain. | Rinse time (SP-09) done, and CT-501 at or below SP-10 | SP-11 | Holding |
| 4 Acid wash | Route supply from the acid tank `<tag>`. Heat to SP-12. Circulate. | TT-501 at or above SP-13 and FT-501 at or above SP-06. Then the acid time (SP-14) is done. | SP-15 | Holding. Abort if the timeout expires. |
| 5 Final rinse | Route supply from the rinse tank. Route return to drain. | CT-501 at or below SP-16 for SP-17 | SP-18 | Holding |
| 6 Finish | Stop P-501, then P-502. Return all valves to the safe lineup. | Pumps stopped, valves in position | SP-19 | Holding |

**7.2.5 Setpoint list (SPL-CIP).** Values are not in the draft except where marked. Process engineering confirms each value.

| ID | Parameter | Value |
|---|---|---|
| SP-01 | Pre-rinse time | 5 min (draft value) |
| SP-07 | Caustic circulation time | 20 min (draft value) |
| SP-09 | Intermediate rinse time | 5 min (draft value) |
| SP-12 | Acid wash temperature | 65 C (draft value) |
| SP-14 | Acid circulation time | 15 min (draft value) |
| SP-02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 08, 10, 11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 | Conductivity limits, temperature limits, minimum flow, step timeouts, final rinse hold time | TBD |

**7.2.6 Abnormal handling**

| Event | Response |
|---|---|
| Bad quality on FT-501, CT-501, or TT-501 | Go to Holding. Raise the alarm. Do not start a step timer. |
| HMI or PLC comms loss | Continue the current step. Do not accept new commands. Go to Holding if loss lasts longer than the comms timeout (TBD). |
| Power loss | Pumps stay stopped. Go to Idle. Do not auto-restart. The operator restarts from Step 1 of the selected circuit. |
| Fail positions | Mix-proof and chemical valves fail closed. Drain valve fail position is TBD (OI-02). |

**7.2.7 Interlocks, alarms, and SIS.** The cause-and-effect chart owns all interlock logic. The alarm database owns all alarms. If a product-separation function is SIS, the SRS owns it. This section does not restate any of them.

**7.2.8 Operator interface.** The HMI shows the selected circuit, state, step, step time, FT-501, TT-501, and CT-501. The operator can select a circuit, start, hold, resume, and abort. The HMI prompts the operator to acknowledge before it resumes from Holding.
